financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone parent) basis. Same period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (segment drivers sit only at Group level; negative-equity/NCI dynamics are Group-level phenomena, NOT present at Company level, since Company total equity is POSITIVE at Rs.63,256,696k, 2025: Rs.63,512,970k -- essentially flat YoY, -0.4%). SHL's standalone Company result is dominated by a large holding-company cost base rather than trading: Company Revenue from contract with customers was Rs.664,044k (+37.5% YoY from Rs.482,966k), but Administrative expenses more than TRIPLED, +205.2% YoY to Rs.371,496k (2025: Rs.121,728k) -- this single line is why Results from operating activities FELL 22.5% YoY to Rs.270,414k (2025: Rs.348,880k) despite the strong revenue growth; the nature of the admin-expense jump is not itemised further in this filing (a genuine disclosure gap, not resolved here). Net finance cost worsened 15.1% YoY to Rs.639,133k (2025: Rs.555,246k) on Finance expenses +13.2% to Rs.1,087,373k. Company PBT loss widened 78.7% YoY to Rs.(368,719)k (2025: Rs.(206,366)k loss); Tax expense is nil both periods. NO EPS IS DISCLOSED AT COMPANY LEVEL in this filing (the Company Income Statement, page 8, has no Loss-per-share line -- only the GROUP Income Statement does) -- eps_basic/eps_diluted are therefore left BLANK for this row, a genuine filing-format gap, not an omission. Investments in subsidiaries (Rs.109,997,148k) is UNCHANGED across all three presented dates (30-Jun-26, 30-Jun-25, 31-Mar-26) -- per the GROUP row's Note 3 citation, this is because management has not yet completed the FY2025/26 fair-value remeasurement of subsidiary investments (Discounted Cash Flow / Net Assets methodology per Note 2), so the Company balance sheet does not yet reflect any change; this is 82.3% of Company Total Assets (Rs.133,613,925k), confirming SHL's standalone balance sheet is fundamentally a holding vehicle. 'Other components of equity' at Company level (Rs.59,190,387k, materially larger than the Group's Rs.9,526,110k) mostly reflects a large Fair value reserve of financial assets at FVOCI relating to the Investments in Subsidiaries measured under SLFRS 9 at Company (unconsolidated) level -- this is why Company total equity (positive, Rs.63,256,696k) is dramatically different from consolidated Group total equity (negative, Rs.(47,624,716)k): the Company's own books value its subsidiary stakes at a large positive fair value, whereas full consolidation nets in each subsidiary's own liabilities and losses -- a genuine and expected holding-company-vs-consolidated divergence, not a data inconsistency. trade_receivables=2,248,208 (Trade and other receivables) EXCLUDES a much larger 'Amounts due from related parties' balance of Rs.19,324,456k (2025: Rs.17,563,101k, +10.0% YoY) -- predominantly intercompany loans/current accounts with subsidiaries, kept separate here as a distinct disclosed line rather than folded into trade receivables. short_term_borrowings=7,160,104 = Current portion of interest bearing borrowings (6,958,454) + Bank overdrafts (201,650); long_term_borrowings=13,653,138 = Interest bearing borrowings (non-current). cash_and_equivalents=47,766 is the face BS 'Cash in hand and at bank'; the Cash Flow Statement shows a NEGATIVE 'Cash and cash equivalents' of Rs.(153,884)k because its 'Analysis of Cash and Cash Equivalents' note (page 11) explicitly nets Bank overdrafts (Rs.201,650k) against cash (Rs.47,766k) -- again an EXPLICITLY RECONCILED definitional difference, not an unresolved gap.

GROUP basis. Softlogic Holdings PLC (SHL) is a large diversified conglomerate reporting seven segments (Note: Operating Segment Information, page 12): Information Technology, Leisure & Property, Retail & Telecommunication, Automobiles, Financial Services (Softlogic Life Insurance/Softlogic Finance), Healthcare Services (Asiri Group of hospitals) and Others -- WITH a genuine 2025 comparator column (unlike JXG/ASPH), so full YoY segment attribution is possible and used throughout this note. Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) vs Q1 FY2025/26 (three months ended 30 June 2025), both presented on the face Income Statement (page 2). CRITICAL BALANCE-SHEET CONTEXT: the Group is in a NET LIABILITY / NEGATIVE EQUITY position -- Total equity was Rs.(47,624,716)k at 30 June 2026 (2025: Rs.(41,944,968)k, deficit widened 13.5% YoY), i.e. Net liability per share of Rs.(51.46) (Note 7.2, page 16) -- this is disclosed by the filing itself, not a data-entry sign error; total_equity is correctly stored as a NEGATIVE number. Equity attributable to parent shareholders was Rs.(71,794,069)k (2025: Rs.(61,936,096)k), partly offset by Non-Controlling Interests of Rs.24,169,353k (2025: Rs.19,991,128k, +20.9% YoY) -- i.e. Group liabilities exceed Group assets, and minority stakes in subsidiaries (chiefly Financial Services and Healthcare Services, which carry material NCI) remain positive even as the consolidated position is negative. Revenue composition: 'Total revenue' (Rs.34,073,784k, +13.5% YoY from Rs.30,013,155k) = Revenue from contract with customers (Rs.21,051,377k, +1.4%) + Revenue from insurance contracts (Rs.12,735,226k, +41.2%) + Interest income (Rs.287,181k, +21.6%) -- the insurance-contract revenue line growing far faster than trading revenue is itself a specific driver of the total. SEGMENT DRIVERS OF THE GROUP RESULT (all YoY, current vs prior quarter, external revenue / PBT unless stated): Financial Services was the dominant driver of Group revenue and operating profit growth -- external revenue +40.2% to Rs.13,136,797k (2025: Rs.9,370,932k), segment operating profit +203.0% to Rs.2,815,742k (2025: Rs.929,508k) -- but segment PBT FELL 28.4% to Rs.491,590k (2025: Rs.686,948k) because the Change in insurance contract liabilities (a required life-fund reserve build tied to new insurance business, presented entirely within this segment) nearly doubled to Rs.3,830,269k (2025: Rs.1,930,334k, +98.4%) -- this single item is why the Group's 106.7% operating-profit surge did NOT translate into a comparable PBT improvement (Group PBT loss only narrowed 3.0%, from Rs.(1,088,844)k to Rs.(1,056,400)k). Healthcare Services (Asiri hospitals) was the largest absolute profit contributor: external revenue +9.1% to Rs.9,521,665k, PBT +7.9% to Rs.1,902,725k, PAT +10.7% to Rs.1,371,633k. Leisure & Property: operating LOSS narrowed 52.4% to Rs.(182,812)k (2025: Rs.(384,278)k) -- an operating improvement -- but segment PBT loss WORSENED 38.6% to Rs.(1,154,875)k (2025: Rs.(833,369)k) because segment Finance expenses more than doubled, +116.1% to Rs.976,337k (2025: Rs.451,873k) -- a leverage/finance-cost-driven deterioration that fully offset the operating gain. Automobiles: external revenue +62.4% YoY to Rs.798,360k (the fastest-growing segment), yet PBT loss widened 164.6% to Rs.(27,697)k (2025: Rs.(10,469)k loss) -- again driven by Finance expenses +58.9% to Rs.61,845k (2025: Rs.38,915k). Information Technology: external revenue FELL 25.1% YoY to Rs.1,161,313k (2025: Rs.1,550,523k), and PBT loss more than doubled to Rs.(187,651)k (2025: Rs.(87,071)k loss) -- the weakest segment on a growth basis. Retail & Telecommunication (largest segment by revenue): external revenue fell 4.7% to Rs.8,954,228k, but PBT loss NARROWED 18.1% to Rs.(1,938,077)k (2025: Rs.(2,367,163)k loss) -- cost discipline improved profitability despite lower sales. PARENT-VS-NCI DIVERGENCE (a specific, quantified point, not generic commentary): Group 'Loss for the period' (total, before split) NARROWED 7.6% YoY to Rs.(1,822,121)k (2025: Rs.(1,972,461)k) -- but Loss attributable to Equity holders of the parent WIDENED 4.8% to Rs.(2,791,497)k (2025: Rs.(2,662,558)k), because Non-Controlling Interests' share of profit grew 40.5% to Rs.969,376k (2025: Rs.690,097k) -- i.e. minority shareholders in the profitable subsidiaries (chiefly Financial Services and Healthcare Services) captured a growing share of the Group's improvement, leaving PARENT shareholders worse off even as the consolidated loss narrowed. profit_after_tax is stored as the Group TOTAL Loss for the period (-1,822,121, ties PBT-tax_expense=PAT for the soft validation check); minority_interest=969,376 is stored separately; eps_basic=(2.00) is based on the PARENT-ONLY loss of (2,791,497) per the face P&L (cross-check: -2,791,497,000/1,395,257,979 shares = Rs.-2.0009/share, matches disclosed -2.00) -- this is a DIFFERENT number from profit_after_tax and the two should not be confused; flagged explicitly here. tax_expense=765,721 (positive magnitude, a genuine expense; -13.3% YoY from Rs.883,617k). Net finance cost worsened 19.2% YoY to Rs.1,418,173k (2025: Rs.1,189,936k) as Finance expenses rose 15.2% to Rs.3,904,862k, partly offset by Finance income +13.1% to Rs.2,486,689k. EBITDA (disclosed on face P&L) was Rs.5,155,202k, +72.7% YoY (2025: Rs.2,985,564k) -- cited for context, not stored (not a schema field). BALANCE SHEET YoY CONTEXT: Insurance contract liabilities (NC) grew 46.7% YoY to Rs.52,213,911k (2025: Rs.35,601,398k), consistent with the Financial Services segment's rapid growth described above. Investment property fell from Rs.1,423,800k (30 June 2025) to Rs.231,700k (30 June 2026), consistent with Rs.1,288,700k of investment-property disposal proceeds recorded in the FY ended 31 March 2026 cash flow column -- i.e. this disposal happened earlier in FY2025/26, not during the current quarter, cited here only to explain the large YoY balance-sheet swing. cash_and_equivalents=11,983,129 is the face BS 'Cash in hand and at bank' line; the Cash Flow Statement's broader 'Cash and cash equivalents' figure of Rs.18,931,493k (Note: Analysis of Cash and Cash Equivalents, page 6) ADDITIONALLY includes Short term investments (Rs.16,859,259k) netted against Bank overdrafts (Rs.9,910,895k) -- this is an EXPLICITLY RECONCILED definitional difference disclosed by the filing itself, not an unresolved discrepancy (unlike the BPPL entry in this database, where a similar gap was NOT explained by any note). short_term_borrowings=32,238,459 = Current portion of interest bearing borrowings (22,327,564) + Bank overdrafts (9,910,895); long_term_borrowings=57,866,071 = Interest bearing borrowings (non-current). Public deposits (current Rs.2,877,586k + non-current Rs.1,192,502k) and Other current financial liabilities (Rs.40,863,929k) are material additional funding/liability lines specific to this financial-services-heavy conglomerate, NOT folded into the borrowings fields to avoid mischaracterisation -- cited here for completeness. depreciation_amortization=1,573,993 = Depreciation of PPE (895,348) + Amortisation of intangible assets (67,812) + Amortisation of ROU assets (610,833), per the cash flow statement (page 5). MATERIAL DISCLOSED GAP (Note 3, Fair Value Measurement, page 13): management is still in the process of measuring the fair value of the Company's investments in subsidiaries as at 31 March 2026 -- 'changes in the fair value of respective subsidiaries of the group for the financial year ended 31 March 2026 have not been reflected in the interim financial statements' -- this affects the COMPANY (standalone) row's Investments in subsidiaries carrying value (unchanged at Rs.109,997,148k across all three presented dates: 30-Jun-26, 30-Jun-25 and 31-Mar-26), a genuine, filing-disclosed valuation lag, not a data gap introduced by this entry. MATERIAL CONTINGENT LIABILITY (Note 8, page 16): an ongoing Inland Revenue dispute over Asiri Surgical Hospital PLC's BOI income-tax exemption for AY2005/06-2014/15, now before the Supreme Court (SC/SPL/LA 69/2026); per LKAS 37 the filing itself declines to quantify the exposure to avoid prejudicing the case. Capital commitments (Note 9) were Rs.8,030.15mn at 30 June 2026 (30 June 2025: Rs.7,559.00mn, +6.2% YoY).

interim_updates.note_text: Softlogic Holdings PLC (SHL) narrowed its Group net loss 7.6% YoY to Rs.1,822.12mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), from Rs.1,972.46mn a year earlier, on Total revenue up 13.5% YoY to Rs.34,073.78mn (2025: Rs.30,013.16mn). By segment (Note: Operating Segment Information, with a genuine 2025 YoY comparator): Financial Services (Softlogic Life Insurance/Softlogic Finance) drove most of the Group's top-line and operating gains -- external revenue +40.2% YoY to Rs.13,136.80mn, segment operating profit +203.0% to Rs.2,815.74mn -- but segment PBT actually FELL 28.4% to Rs.491.59mn (2025: Rs.686.95mn) because the Change in insurance contract liabilities, a required life-fund reserve build tied to new business and presented entirely within this segment, nearly doubled to Rs.3,830.27mn (2025: Rs.1,930.33mn, +98.4%) -- this single item explains why the Group's 106.7% surge in Results from operating activities (to Rs.4,192.04mn) did not translate into a comparable PBT recovery (Group PBT loss only narrowed 3.0%, to Rs.(1,056.40)mn from Rs.(1,088.84)mn). Healthcare Services (Asiri hospitals) was the largest absolute profit contributor and grew steadily: revenue +9.1% to Rs.9,521.67mn, PBT +7.9% to Rs.1,902.73mn, PAT +10.7% to Rs.1,371.63mn. Two smaller segments show a common pattern of operating improvement undone by rising finance costs: Leisure & Property's operating loss narrowed 52.4% to Rs.(182.81)mn, yet its PBT loss WORSENED 38.6% to Rs.(1,154.88)mn because segment finance expenses more than doubled (+116.1% to Rs.976.34mn); Automobiles grew external revenue 62.4% YoY to Rs.798.36mn (the fastest-growing segment) yet its PBT loss widened 164.6% to Rs.(27.70)mn as segment finance expenses rose 58.9% to Rs.61.85mn. Information Technology was the weakest segment: external revenue fell 25.1% YoY to Rs.1,161.31mn and its PBT loss more than doubled to Rs.(187.65)mn. Retail & Telecommunication (the largest segment by revenue) saw external revenue dip 4.7% to Rs.8,954.23mn but its PBT loss NARROWED 18.1% to Rs.(1,938.08)mn, indicating improved cost discipline despite softer sales. A specific, quantified divergence worth flagging: while the Group's TOTAL net loss narrowed 7.6% YoY, the Loss attributable to EQUITY HOLDERS OF THE PARENT actually WIDENED 4.8% YoY to Rs.(2,791.50)mn (2025: Rs.(2,662.56)mn), because Non-Controlling Interests' share of profit grew 40.5% YoY to Rs.969.38mn (2025: Rs.690.10mn) -- i.e. minority shareholders in the profitable Financial Services and Healthcare Services subsidiaries captured a growing share of the Group's improvement, leaving parent shareholders worse off even as the consolidated result improved; reported Basic Loss per Share of Rs.(2.00) (2025: Rs.(1.91)) reflects this parent-only figure, not the smaller Group-total loss. The Group remains in a NET LIABILITY (negative equity) position: Total equity was Rs.(47,624.72)mn at 30 June 2026 (2025: Rs.(41,944.97)mn, deficit widened 13.5% YoY), i.e. Net liability per share of Rs.(51.46) -- a structural balance-sheet feature of this company, not a new development this quarter. Insurance contract liabilities (non-current) grew 46.7% YoY to Rs.52,213.91mn, consistent with the Financial Services segment's rapid growth described above. At standalone COMPANY (parent-only) level, Administrative expenses more than tripled YoY (+205.2% to Rs.371.50mn from Rs.121.73mn), which alone drove a 22.5% decline in Company operating results (to Rs.270.41mn) despite 37.5% Company revenue growth -- the nature of this admin-expense increase is not itemised in the filing. Two disclosed items worth flagging for investors: (1) management has not yet completed its FY2025/26 fair-value remeasurement of investments in subsidiaries (Note 3), so the Company's Rs.109,997.15mn carrying value for those investments is unchanged from a year ago and does not yet reflect any subsidiary performance change; and (2) an ongoing Inland Revenue dispute over Asiri Surgical Hospital PLC's BOI tax exemption (AY2005/06-2014/15) is now before the Supreme Court, with the filing declining to quantify exposure per LKAS 37.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for SHL, no prior quarter collected. profit_after_tax is stored as the Group TOTAL 'Loss for the period' (-1,822,121, before the NCI split, which ties the PBT-tax_expense=PAT soft validation check); this is DIFFERENT from the Rs.(2,791,497)k Loss attributable to equity holders of the parent, which is what eps_basic (-2.00) is actually based on -- both figures are cited and reconciled in the GROUP row's notes and in note_text above, flagged again here so the two are not conflated. No Loss-per-share is disclosed at COMPANY (standalone) level in this filing -- eps_basic/eps_diluted are left blank on the COMPANY row, a genuine filing-format gap. cash_and_equivalents is taken from the face Statement of Financial Position ('Cash in hand and at bank') for both rows; the Cash Flow Statement's broader 'Cash and cash equivalents' figures (Group Rs.18,931,493k; Company Rs.(153,884)k) additionally net in Short term investments and Bank overdrafts per the filing's own 'Analysis of Cash and Cash Equivalents' note -- this is explicitly reconciled by the filing itself, unlike a genuine unexplained gap. The Financial Services segment's Change in insurance contract liabilities is disclosed for the current AND prior-year quarter (a genuine YoY comparison, better than JXG's equivalent single-quarter-only segment disclosure), but no further breakdown by product/policy type is given, so the reserve-build driver could not be decomposed further than the single segment-level figure cited. The nature of the 205.2% YoY jump in Company Administrative expenses is not itemised in the filing -- a genuine disclosure gap, not resolved by this entry.
interim_updates.takeaway: SHL's Group net loss narrowed 7.6% YoY on broad-based revenue growth (+13.5%) led by Financial Services (+40.2% revenue, +203.0% operating profit) and steady Healthcare Services growth (+10.7% PAT), but the headline improvement masks two specific, quantified offsets: a near-doubling of the Financial Services segment's insurance-contract-liability reserve build (+98.4% to Rs.3,830.27mn) capped PBT improvement to just 3.0%, and a 40.5% jump in Non-Controlling Interests' profit share meant parent shareholders' own loss actually WIDENED 4.8% to Rs.2,791.50mn even as the consolidated loss shrank. Leisure & Property and Automobiles both show a similar pattern -- operating-level improvement erased by sharply higher finance expenses (+116.1% and +58.9% respectively) -- flagging balance-sheet leverage as a more binding constraint on those segments than trading performance. The Group's structural net-liability position (Rs.(47,624.72)mn total equity, Net liability per share Rs.(51.46)) and the Company's not-yet-completed fair-value remeasurement of its subsidiary investments (Note 3) are both important standing context for interpreting any quarter's results, not one-off features of Q1 FY2026/27.

operational_highlights: Group Total revenue Rs.34,073.78mn, +13.5% YoY (2025: Rs.30,013.16mn); Group net loss narrowed 7.6% YoY to Rs.1,822.12mn, but Loss attributable to parent equity holders WIDENED 4.8% to Rs.2,791.50mn as NCI profit share grew 40.5% to Rs.969.38mn.

Financial Services segment: external revenue +40.2% YoY to Rs.13,136.80mn, operating profit +203.0% to Rs.2,815.74mn, but segment PBT -28.4% to Rs.491.59mn as the Change in insurance contract liabilities nearly doubled to Rs.3,830.27mn (+98.4% YoY).
Healthcare Services (Asiri) segment: revenue +9.1% to Rs.9,521.67mn, PBT +7.9% to Rs.1,902.73mn, PAT +10.7% to Rs.1,371.63mn -- largest absolute profit contributor.

Leisure & Property and Automobiles both improved operating results but PBT losses WORSENED, driven by finance expenses more than doubling (+116.1% to Rs.976.34mn) and rising 58.9% (to Rs.61.85mn) respectively.
Information Technology segment revenue fell 25.1% YoY to Rs.1,161.31mn, PBT loss more than doubled to Rs.187.65mn -- the weakest segment.
Retail & Telecommunication (largest segment): revenue -4.7% to Rs.8,954.23mn, but PBT loss narrowed 18.1% to Rs.1,938.08mn on improved cost discipline.

Group remains in a net liability position: Total equity Rs.(47,624.72)mn at 30 June 2026, Net liability per share Rs.(51.46); Insurance contract liabilities (non-current) +46.7% YoY to Rs.52,213.91mn.
Company (standalone) Administrative expenses +205.2% YoY to Rs.371.50mn drove a 22.5% decline in Company operating results despite 37.5% Company revenue growth.
key_drivers: Financial Services segment reserve build: Change in insurance contract liabilities +98.4% YoY to Rs.3,830.27mn, absorbing most of the segment's 203.0% operating profit growth and limiting Group PBT improvement to just 3.0% despite a 106.7% operating profit surge.
NCI vs parent divergence: Non-Controlling Interests' profit share +40.5% YoY to Rs.969.38mn caused Loss attributable to parent shareholders to widen 4.8% even as the Group's total loss narrowed 7.6%.
Finance-cost drag in Leisure & Property (+116.1% YoY to Rs.976.34mn) and Automobiles (+58.9% to Rs.61.85mn) turned operating improvements in both segments into worse PBT losses.
Healthcare Services (Asiri) delivered the most consistent absolute profit growth, +10.7% YoY PAT to Rs.1,371.63mn, the largest single profit contributor to the Group.
Company-level Administrative expenses +205.2% YoY (Rs.371.50mn vs Rs.121.73mn) is the primary driver of the standalone parent's 22.5% operating profit decline.
